insights: Gallery has two empirically-verified instances of the conjecture: cos(pi/5) at OQ01OQ02 with r=Y^2-5Y+5 Eisenstein at 5, and cos(pi/7) at OQ01 with r=Y^3-7Y^2+14Y-7 Eisenstein at 7. Both use the substitution Y = 2X + 2 to convert the minimal polynomial of cos(pi/p) into Eisenstein-at-p form.

Cyclotomic-ramification proof of the general conjecture: 2 + 2cos(pi/p) = (1+zeta_{2p})(1+zeta_{2p}^{-1}). Norm computation via Phi_{2p}(-1) = Phi_p(1) = p (using Phi_{2p}(X) = Phi_p(-X) for p odd prime) gives N_{Q(theta_p)/Q}(2+theta_p) = p, so the constant term of the minimal polynomial is plus or minus p, hence has p-adic valuation exactly 1.

Local-field argument: 1 + zeta_{2p} is a uniformizer of the unique prime above p in Z[zeta_{2p}] (totally ramified, e = p-1). Restricting to the real subfield gives ramification index 2 from full cyclotomic, hence v_p(2+theta_p) = 1 in Z[theta_p], i.e., 2+theta_p is a uniformizer at the prime above p in the real subfield. A uniformizer of a totally ramified extension has Eisenstein minimal polynomial; this is the unified proof.

Empirical verification beyond gallery: r_{11}(Y) = Y^5 - 11Y^4 + 44Y^3 - 77Y^2 + 55Y - 11 is Eisenstein at 11 (all sub-leading coefficients are multiples of 11, constant -11 not divisible by 121). r_{13}(Y) = Y^6 - 13Y^5 + 65Y^4 - 156Y^3 + 182Y^2 - 91Y + 13 likewise Eisenstein at 13.

Three formalization levels identified: (1) per-prime enumeration (anti-pattern: just more cases like p=11, 13); (2) parametric statement r_p(Y) with per-prime proof via cyclotomic value-at-1 and Newton identities (recommended for S2); (3) full ramification-theoretic proof using a uniformizer-implies-Eisenstein general lemma (highest-value but Mathlib gap risk).

S6 confirms that the per-prime cyclotomic anchor template (eq_cyclotomic_iff + ring) scales to degree-22 and degree-26 polynomial identities without performance issues. The two ring calls each handle a 4-factor product whose canonical expansion has at most (11)(11) = 121 (for cyclotomic_22) and (13)(13) = 169 (for cyclotomic_26) monomials respectively; both close in normal compilation time.

S6 closes the per-prime cyclotomic-side range to match the full gallery set covered by r_constantCoeff_eq_signed_p (p in {3,5,7,11,13}). Tactic A2 (per-prime extension) is now complete; Tactic A1 (uniform bridge via cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one composed with X -> -X) is the remaining lift target.

Naming convention note: the S5 lemmas used numeric word names cyclotomic_{six,ten,fourteen}_eval_neg_one (because the digit-based names cyclotomic_6_eval_neg_one etc. could parse as identifier prefixes). S6 follows the same convention with cyclotomic_twentytwo_eval_neg_one / cyclotomic_twentysix_eval_neg_one, while the polynomial-equality lemmas use the digit form cyclotomic_22_eq / cyclotomic_26_eq (the trailing _eq makes the digit unambiguous).

S8 closes the uniform bridge identity (cyclotomic (2*p) ℤ) * (X + 1) = X^p + 1 for every odd prime p, eliminating the per-prime ring identities of S5+S6. The proof uses the S7 divisor enumeration as combinatorial input to expand prod_cyclotomic_eq_X_pow_sub_one at n = 2p into a four-term product, then identifies (X-1)·Φ_p = X^p-1 via Mathlib's cyclotomic_prime_mul_X_sub_one and cancels the nonzero X^p-1 factor. Together with S7, Mathlib now has a CLEAN canonical duality Φ_p(X)·(X-1) = X^p-1 vs Φ_{2p}(X)·(X+1) = X^p+1 for p odd prime, exposing Φ_{2p} as the X↦-X conjugate of Φ_p without splitting-field machinery.
